title: Compliance Sprint Cascade: SOC2/ISO Evidence Ownership Roster and Escalation Matrix
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Create an operational 'sprint cascade' for compliance evidence collection and validation that assigns clear ownership for SOC2/ISO artifacts, defines SLAs for evidence delivery, and codifies an escalation matrix for late/missing evidence. This ticket produces a roster (owner, backup, artifact list), a weekly cadence for validation sprints, and an on-call escalation flow for failures that impact audit readiness.

Scope: SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 initial evidence buckets: SSO/SAML setup and logs, audit-log retention pipeline, KMS integration evidence, access reviews, and change-control runbooks. Not in scope: infra-level remediations requiring budget approval (these will be separate ENG tickets).

Deliverables (acceptance criteria):
- Evidence Ownership Roster: CSV + Confluence table listing each evidence artifact, primary owner, backup owner, validation checklist, and expected artifact path. Owner accepts by signing off in Confluence page.
- Weekly Validation Sprint Plan: 6 sprints (2-week cadence) with prioritized artifacts per sprint; each sprint has a defined QA checklist and test harness links.
- Escalation Matrix: steps for 24/48/72 hour slippage with contacts (PM, Eng, Security), automated Slack escalation playbook, and SLA enforcement criteria.
- Measurement Dashboard: a lightweight dashboard widget in Console showing % artifacts validated, overdue items, and blocking risks.

Implementation notes and constraints: Prefix evidence artifacts so automation can pick them up (e.g., evidence/soc2/ssologin/*). For audit-log artifacts we will rely on current logging bucket naming conventions; if gaps found, open ENG remediation tickets. Decision: start with a manual roster process for first two sprints to iterate on artifact taxonomy, then automate ingestion in sprint 3.

Acceptance Criteria: Owner assigned for >=95% of artifacts, first sprint validation completes with <=10% overdue items, escalation playbook tested end-to-end with a simulated missing artifact incident.

Risks: Owner ambiguity for cross-functional artifacts (solution: assign a parent owner and deputies), potential need for infra changes to export historical logs (mitigation: flag as dependency and scope minimal retention export in parallel), and tooling availability for dashboard (use an interim Looker/Metabase query if Console widget not ready).
